speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic. I see you have a history involving gait and limb ataxia; to begin my assessment, how old are you and when did these balance difficulties first start?

speaker: Patient
text: I started having trouble walking recently, and people say I look drunk when I walk. I also feel clumsy in my arms and legs, especially on the right side.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for that description. To narrow down the cause of your ataxia, specifically regarding the right-sided clumsiness and the "drunk" appearance, are your symptoms getting worse over time, or did they start suddenly?

speaker: Patient
text: I have Crohn disease and it has been difficult to control. I have been taking natalizumab for about a year.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Progressive Multifocal Leukoencephalopathy (PML) secondary to natalizumab therapy.

I suspect your recent worsening gait and right-sided ataxia are due to an opportunistic infection of the brain's white matter caused by your immunosuppressant. I need to confirm this immediately.
REQUEST IMAGES: Brain MRI
REQUEST TEST: JC Virus PCR (CSF)
